brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

finish.summary: I built a portable organizer from two cells: a full hex base and a north-half base next to it. The full base holds a removable 3-compartment bin. The half base holds a removable 2-compartment shallow bin, with a drawer on its cut face. Both cells have top covers, and the full-cell cover carries a carry handle. I capped all open faces and bolted the joint between the two bases. The check passes with no rule issues and a "clear" mesh-collision result. That covers fit only. Whether the handle can take the loaded weight depends on the print material, which the configurator doesn't assess. I staged M3 screw, nut and standoff piles in every bin compartment, plus a pile of standoffs in the drawer, and none have prop warnings. You can't see them in a view, though, because the lids are closed. I tried opening the drawer to show its contents, but other props wouldn't fit inside it and the standoffs flagged as floating, so I closed it again. The design has 29 printed parts.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
